learningObjective: Describe the TensorRT deployment pipeline: the builder produces an engine (plan file) from a network description; the runtime loads and executes the engine.
stem: In the TensorRT workflow, which sequence best describes the roles of the builder, engine and runtime?

options.text: The builder and the runtime are the same object in TensorRT; every inference call re-optimizes the graph on the currently observed inputs, which is what allows TensorRT to adapt to shape variations at run time without recompilation.

The builder consumes a network description (e.g., parsed ONNX or the TensorRT network API), runs optimizations (layer fusion, kernel selection, precision calibration) and produces a serialized engine (plan file); the runtime deserializes the engine on the target device and creates an execution context that runs inference.

The engine is a text-format description of the model that the runtime interprets line by line; kernel selection happens on every execution, so plan files are portable across GPUs but slower than a JIT compiler.
TensorRT builds and runs entirely on the CPU; the GPU is only used for peripheral memory transfer, and the actual compute is executed by CUDA-backed CPU kernels that emulate GPU instructions.

explanation: TensorRT's builder is a compile-time component that takes a network description and produces a serialized engine (plan). Optimizations — layer fusion, kernel selection from a tactic set, precision calibration, memory planning — are performed during build. At deployment the runtime deserializes the plan and creates one or more execution contexts that run inference. The plan file is a compiled binary artifact, and it is generally not portable across different GPU architectures without rebuild.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: TensorRT does not re-optimize per inference call.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: standard TensorRT builder → engine → runtime pipeline.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: the plan is binary and pre-optimized; the runtime does not select kernels per call.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: TensorRT executes kernels on the GPU.

assumptions: The user is running the standard TensorRT flow (not TensorRT-LLM's specialized flow, though it is similar).
nonImplications: Does not imply plan files are portable across GPU generations; they are typically architecture- and TRT-version-specific.
Does not imply build time is negligible; large models can take minutes to hours to build.
